claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm happy to help you with your Child Benefit claim for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 18, I need to ask a bit more about his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like A-levels, NVQs, or other qualifications up to and including A-level or equivalent, but not university or higher education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training right now. He finished school and isn't studying at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 18 and not currently in approved education or training, I need to check one more thing.

Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks), or has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation as someone who is not in education, employment, or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with careers service or anything like that. He just finished school and is at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me about Alex, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility.

Unfortunately, based on the Child Benefit rules, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

- Child Benefit is normally available for children **under 16**, or for those **aged 16-19** if they remain in **approved education or training**
- Alex is 18 and has finished school
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation (which could have extended eligibility for up to 20 weeks for 16-17 year olds, but this wouldn't apply as Alex is 18)

Since Alex is 18 and no longer in approved education or training, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to say that based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Summary:**
- Alex is 18 years old and has finished school
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- Child Benefit for children aged 16-19 requires them to be in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs, or equivalent qualifications)
- Since Alex doesn't meet this requirement, he no longer qualifies

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he returns to approved education or training before he turns 20—you may become eligible to claim again at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
